title: Discovery: TempestAI migration from OpenAI to Dedicated
summary: Intro discovery for TempestAI evaluating migration from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated. Key concerns: eval parity, latency and cost tradeoffs, VPC/KMS compliance, compatibility with vLLM/TGI stacks, and pilot benchmarking. Agreed next steps: send Dedicated sizing + pricing, security docs, schedule pilot benchmark run next week.

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-05 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Samir Patel, Evelyn Zhang (Redwood); Lena Ortiz, Marcus Lee, Priya Nair, Jasper (TempestAI)

Auto-generated Summary: Intro call; exploring migration off OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated; deep dive on compatibility and benchmarks.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Samir from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Evelyn our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Lena: Good, thanks. I'm Lena, CTO at Tempest. We cut it to 40 minutes but happy to run longer if needed.
[00:12] Samir: Perfect. Quick agenda: understand your current stack/usages, major constraints, what success looks like, and then go over Redwood Dedicated fit and next steps. Evelyn will jump in on the technicals.
[00:22] Marcus: Quick note: we're running almost everything through OpenAI right now — completion and chat endpoints, a few embeddings. Volume is spiky; monthly spend ~ $65k. Latency is okay generally but we hit slowdowns for long context and batch workloads.
[00:35] Priya: We also have compliance requirements — need SOC2, customer data retention controls, and we want KMS integration for key management.
[00:42] Evelyn: Absolutely - Redwood Dedicated supports VPC and KMS integrations, you can run the private control plane or a VPC peering setup. We'll send the SOC2 and architecture docs after.
[00:50] Lena: Main asks: 1) compatibility - can our existing prompts/evals run unchanged? 2) perf parity with OpenAI models and 3) operational work to get up and running.
[01:02] Samir: Great, that's the crux. On compatibility - we aim to be API-compatible but there are model-to-model differences. For typical generative + chat flows, we map to Redwood-verified open models. For eval parity, we recommend a short benchmark run.
[01:18] Marcus: We're also interested in whether we can reuse our vLLM/TGI-based inference pipeline. We run open weights on prem for some workloads. How does Redwood fit with vLLM or TGI?
[01:30] Evelyn: Redwood's runtime is GPU-optimized and supports serving from several model repos. For on-prem or private deployments, our engine can interop with models used in vLLM/TGI, but the production features — autoscaling, KV cache, compilation/kernels — are part of the Redwood runtime. If you want to keep vLLM locally we can integrate via model compatibility layers but dev/ops work may be higher.
[01:50] Marcus: So there might be differences in latency characteristics between our self-hosted vLLM and Redwood Dedicated?
[01:55] Evelyn: Yes — vLLM/TGI performance depends on your tuning and hardware. Redwood picks kernels and batching strategies to optimize tail latency and cost. For short-turn chat, Dedicated often beats naive self-hosted setups because of continuous batching and optimized KV cache handling.
[02:12] Lena: Can you speak to eval parity — like hallucination rates and output distribution? If we switch models we need to make sure higher-level behavior is consistent.
[02:20] Samir: We always recommend running your existing eval suite against candidate models on Redwood. We have a Redwood-verified model catalog and will run the same prompts through the comparison harness. Evelyn will share the harness.
[02:31] Evelyn: Also worth noting quantization profiles: if you move to 4-bit quantized variants you might see subtle behavior shifts. We'll surface that in the results.
[02:42] Jasper: Any limitations on function calling or streaming? Our product relies on streaming partial responses.
[02:47] Evelyn: Streaming and function/tool calling are supported; we do the same chunked streaming interface and have guidance for reducing latency with prefix caching.
[02:56] Priya: Security: we use AWS KMS and need support for customer-managed keys and audit logs. Can Redwood Dedicated do that in VPC mode?
[03:05] Samir: Yes — Dedicated supports KMS/HSM integrations and has audit log export. For private/on-prem we offer a packaged option. We'll attach the architecture diagram and SOC2 artifacts.
[03:15] Marcus: Ops question: how much effort is onboarding? We want to estimate dev/ops time.
[03:19] Samir: Typical pilot to production takes 4-8 weeks depending on complexity. Pilot is usually a small subset of traffic and we run a benchmark to align perf/cost. For your size, I expect a 2-4 week pilot plus integration.
[03:33] Lena: Cost — our CFO will push back. How do you compare cost per token vs OpenAI?
[03:38] Samir: Hosted API pricing is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity which can be more cost-effective at scale. We'll provide a sizing estimate and a cost model. It's a tradeoff: Dedicated is upfront commit but gives predictable unit economics.
[03:51] Marcus: We use a lot of long context chains (20k+ tokens) — how do you handle KV cache and memory?
[03:58] Evelyn: Our runtime supports KV cache management and sequence length aware kernel selection. For very long context, we recommend model variants and quantization profiles tuned for memory. We'll recommend setups in the sizing doc.
[04:12] Lena: Any pitfalls with migrating evals? We want minimal regression risk.
[04:17] Evelyn: Regression risk is real — small behavior differences can occur. Best practice is A/B testing and running your eval harness across the top 2-3 candidate models. We also provide quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[04:34] Marcus: Does Redwood support embeddings into our vector DB? We currently use OpenAI embeddings and a managed vector store.
[04:40] Samir: Yes — embeddings are supported, same export patterns. If you want to keep your vector DB, we'll maintain identical vector dimensions for compatible models, otherwise you may need to reindex for a different encoder.
[04:54] Jasper: If we do a Dedicated pilot, can we route only a percentage of production traffic?
[04:59] Samir: Absolutely. We support canary and traffic-splitting rollouts and automatic fallback to hosted variants if Dedicated capacity is constrained.
[05:10] Priya: Network egress and data residency — we need EU-only residency for some customers.
[05:16] Evelyn: Dedicated clusters can be provisioned in specific regions and we support data locality controls. For Private on-prem deployments, you can keep everything in your network.
[05:26] Lena: Ok let's do a quick recap and concrete next steps.
[05:30] Samir: Recap: Redwood to send sizing/pricing, security docs, and the benchmark harness. Tempest to share usage logs and eval prompts. Schedule pilot kickoff for next week.
[05:40] Marcus: Sounds good. One more technical: does Redwood expose metrics and token-level cost breakdowns?
[05:45] Evelyn: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost, latency breakdown, per-route dashboards, and tracing. We'll give you a demo access on the pilot cluster.
[05:56] Lena: Great. Any blockers on our side? We'll confirm internal stakeholders and legal baseline — procurement will need the SOC2 and contract terms.
[06:06] Samir: We'll include the compliance pack. Also, Evelyn will send a sample benchmark runbook.
[06:12] Jasper: Would be helpful to see a sample results sheet comparing OpenAI to Redwood candidate models on our prompts.
[06:18] Evelyn: We'll run an initial pass once you share the top prompts and logs — that will show eval parity and latency numbers.
[06:25] Samir: Perfect. I'll follow up with the pricing and a proposed pilot plan. Thanks everyone.
[06:30] Lena: Thanks, appreciate it.
[06:32] End of call.

Notes: transcription includes occasional mislabels; some words auto-corrected (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cache").
